Commonwealth Games live updates: Fastest man and woman to be crowned in 100m, Diamonds take on Malawi
After four consecutive days of brilliance for Australia's Commonwealth Games athletes, there is more to come on day five with the men's and women's 100m semifinals and finals.
The netball is back in action with the Diamonds taking on Malawi in their third group game and Kyle Chalmers will aim for gold in the men's 100m freestyle.
Follow all the action in our live blog.

Live updates
Tue 28 Jul 2026 at 6:46pm
Weightlifting: Ryven Ewing in action first up
To the Armadillo!
Never thought I'd be writing that in a sport's blog, but here we are...
Anyway, we're hitting the ground running straight away with morning, with Ryven Ewing in action in the men's 88kg weight lifting category.
Lovely story for the UQ student.
Ewing was, in fact, born in Scotland and was raised there until he was 8.
"It'll be so special for people who have been such an important part of my journey to be there and watch," Ewing said told UQ before the Games.
"It feels like I'm bringing two different worlds together."
The 24-year-old, who is studying for a Master of Physiotherapy, used to play rugby but transitioned to weightlifting as a was to improve himself.
"Physiotherapy and weightlifting complement each other really well," he said.
"Both are about understanding how the human body moves, and that knowledge definitely helps me as an athlete and as a clinician.
"Technique is a massive part of weightlifting - sometimes I wish it was just brute strength, but there are lots of small technical details that can help you make much better use of your strength.
"For me, weightlifting is less about beating other people and more about trying to be better than I was.
"If I can improve on my own performances, I know I'll usually end up in a pretty good position."
Tue 28 Jul 2026 at 6:38pm
Hello everyone
Good day to you all and welcome to the ABC Sport coverage of the fifth day of action from the 2026 Commonwealth Games.
My name is Simon Smale and I am here with Gemma Ferguson on this side of the world, while Jon Healy is over there in Glasgow, enjoying the festival of sport first hand.
I know we're feeling the love and the vicarious thrill of gold on behalf of our amazing competitors so far, so I hope you are too.
Another busy day of action, with swimming and athletics heats this morning, some big 3X3 wheelchair basketball matches, more medal prospects in the gymnastics, a bronze medal bowls contest, a couple of boxing bouts, weightlifting and the netball.
A bit on, as they say.
We'll be here throughout the night and into the morning to guide you through it all.

Commonwealth Games: Lachlan Kennedy and Torrie Lewis break Australian 100m national records, Eleanor Patterson wins gold in high jump
Eleanor Patterson won her second Commonwealth Games gold medal in the women's high jump on day five in Glasgow, leading home an Australian 1-2 on another stunning day for Australia.
Patterson was one of nine Australian gold medal performances, taking the team to 35 gold medals for the Games so far.
Twelve years after first triumphing in Glasgow as a teenager, Patterson equalled the Games record of 1.96m in a rain-interrupted final.
She managed the height with her third and last attempt before unsuccessfully attempting a new Games mark of 2m.
Patterson edged out Australian teammate and world champion, Nicola Olyslagers (1.93m).
Olyslagers failed with her three attempts at 1.96m and settled for silver.
On a big night at the main stadium, Lachie Kennedy and Torrie Lewis both missed out on gold, but broke 100m national records while capturing medals.
Kennedy ended Australia's agonising wait for a men's Commonwealth Games 100m medal by taking silver.
Australia's fastest man ran a personal best 9.85 seconds, beating Patrick Johnson's mark of 9.93 set in May 2003. It took a Games record to beat Kennedy, with Cameroon's Emmanuel Eseme stopping the clock at 9.83.
Nigeria's Kayinsola Ajayi (9.90) was third, with Australian Eddie Nketia (10.06) back in sixth.
Lewis broke her own 100m national record in the semi-finals then broke it again in the final, finishing third in 10.99.
New Zealander Zoe Hobbs (10.93) won gold ahead of England's Amy Hunt (10.98).
Kennedy's silver was Australia's first medal in the men's 100m since 1962, when Michael Cleary took bronze.
Kennedy broke 10 seconds and lowered his personal best twice on the night, including a 9.94 in his semi, despite wet and windy conditions.
"It's all about rising to the occasion," Kennedy said after a wet and windy night.
"I'm a big believer in you've got to bring your best when it matters most. That's what we've been training for all season.
"To be able to come out here in those conditions, against a field like that, and to be able to run a time like that just goes to show how much faith I have in my team and all the people supporting me back home."
There was also joy for Ky Robinson, who completed an unprecedented 10,000m double for Australia when he finished strongly to hold off several rivals and claim gold.
Robinson won in 27:48.93 ahead of India's Gulveer Singh and Isle of Man's David Mullarkey.
His triumph followed Rose Davies becoming the first Australian woman to win the event at the Commonwealth Games.
In the pool, Lani Pallister set a new Commonwealth Games record in winning her third gold of the meet.
Pallister won the 800m freestyle in a time of 8:11:12, beating New Zealand's Erika Fairweather.
Australia's Molly Walker took the bronze.
Pallister has now won the freestyle middle and distance triple - the 400, 800 and 1,500m freestyle.
In all, Australia won a total of five gold medals in the night session at Tollcross Swimming Centre.
Catch up on all the action from day five of the Games in our blog below.
AAP/ABC

Diamonds dazzle against Malawi
The Diamonds have a trifecta of wins to start their campaign at the 2026 Commonwealth Games.
They get the win comfortably against Malawi, 68-32.
Here's what captain Liz Watson had to say after the game:
"We had to stay patient; I'm really proud we could get the win," she says.
"Credit to Malawi, they brought the physicality. I think to have a scoreline like that is great for us."
But all eyes will be on tomorrow's game as the two undefeated sides of Australia and South Africa meet.
So, make sure to tune in from 6am AEST. You don't want to miss it!
And how's this for an awesome stat!
Wed 29 Jul 2026 at 7:28am
Athletics: Kennedy feeling 'very proud'
Lachlan Kennedy has spoken to reporters in the mixed zone.
When asked how he was feeling after winning silver, Kennedy said:
Good. Relief. To be able to come out here in those conditions against a field like that and to be able to run a time like that, it just goes to show the faith I have in my team and all the people supporting me back home.
Pride, I guess. Very proud for my country to be able to get them a medal in the Comm Games. Big relief, big relief.
Kennedy was asked how he performed under pressure:
It's all about rising to the occasion, I'm a big believer in you've got to bring your best when it matters most.
So that's what we've been training for all season. We've all been planning for this comp here and my coach (Andrew Iselin) has clearly outdone himself.
Kennedy was also asked about how the Australian squad was performing in Glasgow:
Aussie track [and field] is clearly in the best spot it's ever been. Our team is so strong.
Two Aussie sprint medals? that's crazy at the Comm Games. We're in a real golden age, there's a lot of youngsters, a lot of good veteran talent as well.
I'm just honoured to be a part of the team.
